subject: Post-call recap: Data protection & logging constraints for MedicoPilot
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Singh <anika.s@medico.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.b@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap: Data protection & logging constraints for MedicoPilot

Hi Anika / Rajiv — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side with the items we agreed and open questions so we can align next steps. I pulled this together to make sure everyone (including our engineering team) is aligned on the privacy/logging constraints you highlighted.

Key pain points you shared
- Live inference touches PHI/PII (patient names, MRN) and CANNOT be stored in raw logs.
- Current audit requirements: immutable audit trail for all inference requests + response metadata (but not raw prompt text).
- Retention window: 90 days for request/response metadata, 0 days for any PII in logs unless explicitly redacted.
- Redaction: must support deterministic redaction of emails/SSNs in-line and also a configurable post-processing hook to remove tokens flagged as PII.

Current stack you described
- Ingestion/telemetry: self-hosted Fluentd -> S3 (encrypted)
- Models: on-prem weights behind internal API gateway (Kube cluster)
- Auth/keys: central KMS (customer-managed)

Success criteria you mentioned
- No PII persisted in any Redwood-hosted or third-party logs by default.
- Retention and audit logs accessible to your security team for 90 days.
- Ability to run an access audit (who queried what) and export that to CSV for compliance.

Agreed actions / next steps
1) I will share our redaction pattern recommendations and a short design note outlining where Redwood can enforce PII redaction vs where it must be handled by MedicoPilot (see attachments). (Ava) — by EOD Tue 4/13
2) Technical deep-dive with your infra/security (we suggested 60–90 minute session). Can you propose 2 windows Wed/Thu next week? (Anika/Rajiv)
3) I’ll pull SOC2 + current audit playbook and a sample logging policy for private deployments. (Monica) — shared after deep-dive
4) Draft mutual action plan and prescriptive rollout (proof-of-concept -> canary -> prod). (Dylan + Ava)

Open questions we left on the call
- Do you require HSM-backed key storage for model encryption-at-rest, or is customer KMS acceptable?
- For redaction: is deterministic regex-based removal sufficient for your use-case, or do you need ML-based PII detection with human review?

Attachments: MedicoPilot-PII-requirements-v1.pdf (requirements doc), redaction-examples.xlsx (sample strings + regexes).

If that looks right I’ll schedule the deep-dive once you confirm available times. Thanks — appreciated the clarity on constraints; it helps us scope the private deployment options.

— Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Anika Singh <anika.s@medico.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Patel <r.patel@medico.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.b@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.p@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 18:24:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Data protection & logging constraints for MedicoPilot

Thanks Ava — clear and helpful. A couple of clarifications:
1) KMS: customer-managed KMS is acceptable; HSM not required for PoC but will be a requirement for Tier 1 production (45–90 days roadmap).
2) Redaction: deterministic regex catches ~85% of cases (emails, SSNs). We would like ML-based PII detection for free-text fields where regex fails; initially batch review is fine, but plan should include human-in-the-loop for edge cases.
3) Audit exports: yes, prefer CSV with columns (timestamp, user_id, model_version, route, action_type).

Availability for deep-dive:
- Wed 4/14: 11:00–12:30 ET
- Thu 4/15: 15:00–16:30 ET

Please schedule for Wed 11:00 ET if that works for your team. Also, thanks for the attachments — I’ll review and flag anything missing.

Best,
Anika
Head of Data Protection | MedicoPilot
Anika.S@medico.com
